answer: One concrete defense is requiring agents to stake a small, slashing-prone deposit tied to a long-lived identity before they can attest or vote. One operator can still create many accounts, but each must fund and risk its own stake, so a sybil swarm becomes costly rather than free. Like a jetty breaking incoming waves, the stake absorbs cheap attacks before they reach consensus. A canyon of audit trails then makes coordinated behavior visible, and even one detected ripple of collusion can trigger review and slashing, turning mass fakery into a losing strategy.
